subject: Marketplace listing preflight: branding, claims & support window mapping
messages:
From: Michael Evans <michael.evans@cloudpulse.com>

Cc: Anna Ruiz <anna.ruiz@cloudpulse.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace listing preflight: branding/claims & support window mapping

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for taking this — CloudPulse is preparing AWS and Azure catalog entries and we want to make sure we don't hit any last-minute policy holds. Two quick asks to start:

1) Branding & claims: We currently call out “Continuous 99.95% uptime” and “24/7 enterprise support” in the marketing copy. Can you confirm what phrasing will pass AWS/Azure marketplace review? Any required footnote language or limits on uptime claims?

2) Support windows: We need to map our existing support schedule to the marketplace support tiers. Attached is our internal support-hours-matrix.xlsx showing regional coverage. Can you confirm if the marketplace requires specific response targets or regional support buckets for co-sell eligibility?

I've attached the product spec PDF and the support matrix for context. If helpful, Anna (cc) can walk through the matrix. Ideally we want a short list of 'must-fix' items so the content team can iterate today.

Thanks — appreciate a quick read.

—Michael
Head of Alliances, CloudPulse Inc.
attachments: CloudPulse_Marketplace_Catalog_Specs.pdf (pdf), support-hours-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing preflight: branding/claims & support window mapping

Michael — thanks for the materials and the clear asks. Looping in Logan, Kimberly and Jonas to cover ops, legal, and co-sell policy.

Quick summary / next steps from our side:
- Branding & claims: We cannot use absolute language like “always” or “continuous” without a qualifying SLA footnote. For marketplace copy we recommend: "99.95% availability (subject to scheduled maintenance and force majeure)" and a short footnote linking to your SLA PDF. Kimberly will confirm any trademark/logo labeling requirements.
- Support windows: Marketplace programs typically map to three tiers (Standard, Business, Enterprise). For co-sell you should map to Business or Enterprise and provide target response times (P1 1 hour, P2 4 hours, P3 24 hours) and regional coverage. Jonas — see Logan's ask below for a specific matrix mapping.
- Evidence required: signed logo license, screenshot of support portal with escalation paths, SOC2 summary (if you have one), and the support-hours-matrix.xlsx that you already sent.

Can you upload the signed logo license and SOC2 summary to the Drive link below? We should be able to turn around a short compliance checklist within 48–72 hours once we have those items.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBxyz-marketplace-preflight

If you want, we can hop on a 30-min call this afternoon to triage — otherwise we'll send a consolidated preflight checklist by EOD.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Marketplace Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: CloudPulse listing - compliance items and suggested copy

Team — quick internal roundup after reading Michael's specs:

1) Claims language (legal + marketplace):
- Replace "Continuous 99.95% uptime" with "99.95% availability (see SLA)". Avoid ranking language like "best-in-class" and any comparative statements unless substantiated by public benchmarks.
- Add footnote: "Availability measured monthly; scheduled maintenance windows excluded. See full SLA at <link>".

2) Branding/assets: 
- Need signed-logo-license.pdf (explicit permission for marketplace use).
- Confirm whether CloudPulse wants "Offered by CloudPulse" (Azure/GCP) vs "Sold by" (AWS co-sell) copy; AWS requires marketplace vendor account mapping.

3) Support mapping (proposal to send externally):
- Proposed mapping table for Michael:
  * Standard — Business hours only (P1 8h, P2 24h)
  * Business — 24x5 (P1 4h, P2 8h)
  * Enterprise — 24x7 (P1 1h, P2 4h)
- For co-sell options, require Enterprise tier or documented escalation path into vendor and cloud partner; otherwise co-sell may be restricted.

4) Evidence checklist to request from CloudPulse: logo license, SOC2 Type II summary (redacted), support runbook screenshot, and the signed partner agreement or marketplace onboarding doc.

5) Policy quirks for multi-cloud:
- Azure/GCP have more relaxed brand copy but still prohibit uptime absolutes.
- Be explicit about region mapping: if CloudPulse does not staff APAC overnight, they must avoid saying "24/7 global support"; instead specify regional coverage.

I'll draft suggested copy and a minimal checklist for Tessa to send back. Jonas — can you run the co-sell eligibility check (AWS partner account mapping) and flag any gating items?

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Partner Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
